questions.prompt: What is the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) in JavaScript?

options.text: The duration during which a browser tab is suspended in the background.
The time between the creation of a block scope and the actual execution of a let or const declaration where accessing the variable throws a ReferenceError.
A garbage collection cycle that cleans up circular object references.
The time spent waiting for an asynchronous network fetch to resolve.

questions.explanation: The TDZ begins when the block execution context is created and ends when the variable's declaration line is executed.

questions.prompt: What error occurs when a function calls itself indefinitely without a base case in JavaScript?

options.text: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded

questions.explanation: Every function call adds a frame to the V8 call stack. When available stack memory is exhausted, V8 raises a RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.

questions.prompt: What enables a JavaScript closure to access variables of a parent function after the parent has returned?

options.text: Variables are copied into the browser's localStorage.
The garbage collector retains the parent function's lexical environment on the heap because the inner function holds an active reference to it.
JavaScript converts the outer function into an asynchronous Promise.
Variables are permanently registered in the global Window object.

questions.explanation: Mark-and-sweep garbage collection traces active references. Since the inner function references the parent's lexical scope, the parent environment cannot be collected.

questions.prompt: What is a common performance hazard when creating closures inside event listeners without cleanup?

options.text: Memory leaks caused by retaining references to parent objects or DOM nodes long after they are needed.

questions.explanation: If a closure retains a reference to an outer object (e.g. large arrays or DOM elements) and the listener is never removed, garbage collection cannot reclaim that memory.
